task.description: Hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's design artefact for ISS-0430, lib/letflow/design/iss0430-notify-listen-decision.md. Read docs/issues/ISS-0430.yaml in full for the 8 acceptance criteria and 5 named design questions. Independently re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself and from the real source files it cites -- do NOT accept CODE-DESIGNER's own claims about supervision-tree ordering or poller mechanics without checking them yourself against lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex, and lib/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure.ex directly (per core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step' -- a validator that only reads the producer's own summary has not validated anything). Specifically verify: (1) the claimed placement (new child of Infrastructure, immediately after Repo/Ecto.Migrator, before Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker) does not contradict ISS-0429's or ISS-0451's already-documented ordering/restart-intensity guarantees -- read those modules' own moduledocs yourself; (2) the tenant-isolation mechanism (Question 2's 'option (a), opaque routing id, receiver re-derives its own :prefix scope') is reasoned concretely against decision 0003 Dimension B's actual mechanism, not asserted; check that the per-tenant sequential-id enumeration argument (schema-per-tenant means disjoint per-schema id sequences) is factually sound given Letflow's actual schema-per-tenant migration strategy; (3) all 8 ACs are individually satisfied -- go through each AC from ISS-0430.yaml by name and state a verdict against it; (4) no implementation code (.ex bodies, runnable migrations) is present -- the Question 3 schema sketch and Question 1's illustrative wrapper description are the two places most likely to have drifted into implementation, check both specifically; (5) the design's own self-reported correction (Question 5's ISS-0031 mis-citation) is itself accurate -- briefly confirm docs/issues/ISS-0031.yaml really is unrelated, as claimed. This is a hard gate: if any AC is unmet or any claim about existing source doesn't check out, FAIL with the specific gap named (per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail worked example), not a general impression.
acceptance_criteria: Each of ISS-0430's 8 acceptance criteria individually verdicted (met/not met) against the artefact
Supervision-tree placement claim independently checked against lib/letflow/application.ex and the two supervisor modules' own moduledocs, not merely trusted
Tenant-isolation mechanism (Question 2) independently checked for concrete reasoning against decision 0003, not accepted on the producer's assertion alone
Confirms no implementation code (.ex bodies, runnable migration DDL) is present in the artefact
Confirms the Question 5 ISS-0031 self-correction is itself accurate
PASS or FAIL stated with specific evidence either way; on FAIL, next_action names CODE-DESIGNER for rework with the exact gaps

result.summary: PASS. Independently re-derived against lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure.ex, docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md, and docs/issues/ISS-0031.yaml directly (not the artefact's or the diagnosis handoff's summaries). SUPERVISION PLACEMENT: confirmed accurate. application.ex:62-67 lists [Infrastructure, Supervisor.child_spec(Pollers, restart: :temporary), PollersBreaker, Http]; Infrastructure's own moduledoc lines 14-16 confirm children 1-3 are Letflow.Repo, Ecto.Migrator, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker -- matching the artefact's claimed placement (new child after infra child 2, before child 3). ISS-0429's guarantee (Infrastructure moduledoc lines 41-51, 'Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor is the LAST child... supervisor-boundary guarantee') is unaffected because the new child sits earlier in Infrastructure's own list, still strictly before the Infrastructure->Pollers supervisor boundary. ISS-0451's restart:temporary override (pollers.ex moduledoc lines 15-46) is scoped to Pollers specifically; Infrastructure keeps plain OTP-default restart intensity per its own moduledoc (lines 8-10) -- the artefact correctly does not apply ISS-0451's guarantee to a child placed in Infrastructure. No contradiction found. TENANT ISOLATION (Q2): reasoned concretely against 0003 Dimension B's actual text (lines 37-45, 216-225: schema-per-tenant via Ecto :prefix, no session/connection-level tenant context, Addendum lines 326-396 explicitly rejects a GUC mechanism) -- not asserted. The opaque-routing-id/receiver-re-derives-:prefix mechanism is a sound response to NOTIFY's database-global, schema-blind delivery (Postgres does not consult :prefix/search_path when routing NOTIFY, which the artefact states and which is consistent with Postgres's documented behavior). The disjoint-per-schema-sequence claim is factually sound given decision 0003's schema-per-tenant description (separate physical tables per schema each carry their own PK sequence object) -- checked against 0003's own text describing real per-schema table provisioning (lines 143-181), not just accepted on the artefact's assertion. IMPLEMENTATION CODE: confirmed absent. Checked Question 1's wrapper description (prose only, explicitly 'illustrative name... not implemented here'), Question 3's schema sketch (a markdown field-name table plus descriptive prose, no code block, no defmodule/def), and Question 5's test strategy (numbered prose steps naming functions like Sandbox.checkout/1, no actual .exs content) -- the two places flagged as most likely to drift into implementation are both clean; no .ex body or migration DDL anywhere in the document. ISS-0031 SELF-CORRECTION: confirmed accurate by reading docs/issues/ISS-0031.yaml directly -- it is a :telemetry.attach/4 cross-process message-leak fix in tenant_status_test.exs (resolved 2026-08-17), unrelated to DDL visibility or non-sandboxed-connection testing technique, exactly as the artefact states. ALL 8 ACs FROM ISS-0430.yaml VERDICTED INDIVIDUALLY, ALL MET: (1) all 5 design questions answered explicitly -- MET. (2) Postgres remains source of truth, payload is routing-hint-only/untrusted -- MET (Q2/Q3, invariant I2). (3) polling explicitly retained, both intervals named (5000ms each, matching the diagnosis handoff's verified defaults) -- MET (Q4). (4) tenant isolation addressed as security property with named mechanism and SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off explicitly flagged for implementation time -- MET (Q2, lines 336-340; appropriate for a design-only artefact per ISS-0430's own 'implementation is separate follow-on work' scope note). (5) reconciled with current supervision tree, LISTEN connection given a stated place, not an unplaced peer -- MET, independently confirmed above. (6) relationship to both shipped pollers stated explicitly (NOT NOW, argued) -- MET (Q6). (7) performance claim justified by eliminated round trips, notes ~92% Docker Desktop overhead and ~0.11ms co-located figure -- MET (Q6 'AC7' subsection, matches ISS-0430.yaml's own filed profiling numbers exactly). (8) no consumer implementation included -- MET, independently confirmed above.
